dedupe_keys.name: cross border transport layers of the greater region gis gr bus lines railway lines and cycle paths

description: The Geographic Information System of the Greater Region (GIS-GR) harmonises spatial data across the borders of Luxembourg and the neighbouring regions of France, Germany and Belgium for cross-border territorial observation and planning. Its transport layers include cross-border bus lines, stops and park-and-ride sites at the Greater Region's internal borders (situation September 2015, compiled from Citéline, the Transport Community, TEC, Mobiregio and the Greater Region transport working group), cross-border railway lines and stations (September 2015, from DB, CFL, SNCB and SNCF), and European and cross-border cycle paths (2026 edition, from EuroVelo, biroto, Luxembourg for Tourism, Saarland and Walloon sources). The layers are published on Luxembourg's open data portal data.public.lu as GeoJSON, shapefile or GeoPackage downloads with WMS services and a web map, free under CC BY; the portal entries were refreshed in 2026. The GIS-GR transport theme also covers carpooling, charging points, infrastructure and accessibility maps. Caveats: the bus and rail layers show 2015 services and have no timetables or frequencies; they cover only lines crossing internal borders; and harmonisation choices are not documented in the entries. The layers support network flow and capacity studies of cross-border commuting, such as building a multimodal border network for the Luxembourg labour market; related records are the JRC cross-border road accessibility grid and the Mobility Database.
